teams.heading: Ben Spencer emerges as November doubt for England after shoulder surgery
teams.body: Steve Borthwick faces a major scrum-half dilemma after Ben Spencer was ruled out of the start of the Premiership season. Bath confirmed the 34-year-old underwent shoulder surgery to address a long-standing issue following England’s summer tour. While Spencer is expected to return later in the autumn, he is now in a race against time to prove his fitness before November's Nations Championship Tests. In his absence, Borthwick will likely lean on Alex Mitchell and Jack van Poortvliet as his primary options for the autumn campaign.

lead.why: Ben Spencer is a serious doubt for England's autumn internationals after undergoing shoulder surgery.

teams.heading: Jack Crowley ruled out of November internationals with vascular injury
teams.body: Ireland fly-half Jack Crowley has been ruled out of action until the new year, delivering a major selection blow ahead of the November internationals. Munster head coach Clayton McMillan confirmed the 26-year-old is still recovering from a lower-limb vascular injury suffered in April. Having missed July's tests, Crowley will now sit out the upcoming clashes against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa. McMillan emphasised the recovery is the main focus, stating, "ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority."

lead.why: Jack Crowley being ruled out until the new year is a major blow to Ireland's fly-half options for the November internationals.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi names unchanged Argentina starting team to face Australia
teams.body: Los Pumas head coach Felipe Contepomi has named an unchanged starting XV for Saturday's first Test against Australia in Jujuy, backing the side that pushed South Africa close in a 17-10 defeat. Pablo Matera continues as captain in the absence of Julián Montoya, who remains unavailable alongside Marcos Kremer and Mateo Carreras. The only adjustments come on the bench, where Contepomi has opted for a 5-3 split, bringing in Rodrigo Martínez and Nicolás Roger.

teams.heading: Les Kiss drops Harry Wilson and benches Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii for Argentina
teams.body: Wallabies head coach Les Kiss has made the bold call to rotate his entire starting forward pack for Saturday's Test against Argentina in Jujuy, resting captain Harry Wilson completely. Allan Alaalatoa takes over the captaincy, while fit-again recruit Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii must settle for a place on the bench as Kiss seeks to build squad depth ahead of the 2027 World Cup. "I need to know that I’ve got two good XVs," Kiss explained. Isaac Kailea also returns to start at prop for his first international appearance since 2024.

lead.why: The wholesale rotation of the Wallabies forward pack and the complete omission of captain Harry Wilson represents the most significant tactical decision ahead of the Argentina Test.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One scraps controversial restrictions on naturalised Brave Blossoms
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has abandoned plans to restrict naturalised players in matchday squads following a legal settlement with 25 professionals. The proposed system would have categorised foreign-born athletes without six years of Japanese schooling differently from domestic-born players, even those with citizenship. Under the agreement reached at the Tokyo District Court, naturalised stars like Timothy Lafaele and Jiwon Gu will retain their primary registration status. The league admitted that its prior communication with players was "insufficient" after the group alleged the rules threatened their professional livelihoods.

lead.why: Significant legal settlement reversing a controversial eligibility rule that affected several high-profile Japan internationals.

teams.heading: Anton Segner ruled out of South Africa tour following ankle surgery
teams.body: Anton Segner has become the fifth New Zealand player to be ruled out of the current tour following surgery on an infected ankle. The flanker, who debuted in July, will remain with the squad in Cape Town but will not feature in the remaining matches. Despite losing him alongside four other squad members including Caleb Clarke and Billy Proctor, coach Dave Rennie will not call up a replacement. Rennie remains confident in his loose forward depth as his unbeaten side prepares for today’s second Test against South Africa.

lead.why: The tour-ending injury to Anton Segner, the fifth player to be sent home, is the most prominent New Zealand story today with high corroboration.

teams.heading: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu replaces Handré Pollard for South Africa’s vital Cape Town Test
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has been forced into a late fly-half adjustment after Handré Pollard failed a fitness test on the eve of the second Test against New Zealand. Pollard, initially selected to anchor a conservative gameplan, suffered a "niggle" during training. His withdrawal elevates 24-year-old Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu to the starting No. 10 jersey as the Springboks seek to level the series following their 33-16 defeat in Johannesburg. Elsewhere, Cheslin Kolbe returns to the wing for the must-win encounter at Cape Town Stadium.
